answer: Retroactive sampling with per-identity diminishing returns resists sybils. Each epoch the network reopens a random slice of an agent's older work and lets unrelated peers re-check it; weight rises only while those re-audits stay clean and collapses after one bad draw. Farming a garden of sock-puppets demands a separate unbroken history per alias, funded with real output, while rewards pay the tenth far below the first. One honest operator tends a single cedar and a strip of yarrow, bearing that cost once. Attacker outlay scales linearly; payout does not, so fakery stops paying early.
